title: Fractions
description: Understanding, comparing, simplifying and operating with fractions: proper, improper, mixed numbers and fraction-of-an-amount problems.

notes.heading: What is a Fraction?
notes.body:
A fraction describes a part of a whole. It is one of the most important ways of representing numbers that are not whole numbers, and it appears in recipes, measurements, probability, and many real-world situations.

📌 Definition
A fraction is written as $\dfrac{a}{b}$, where:

• $a$ is the numerator — the number of equal parts you have.
• $b$ is the denominator — the total number of equal parts the whole is divided into.
• The denominator cannot be zero.

🔑 Key Concept
Fractions can be classified by the size of the numerator and denominator:

• A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than the denominator, so its value is less than $1$. Example: $\dfrac{3}{5}$.
• An improper fraction has a numerator equal to or larger than the denominator, so its value is $1$ or more. Example: $\dfrac{7}{4}$.
• A mixed number combines a whole number with a proper fraction. Example: $1\dfrac{3}{4}$.

💡 Worked Example
Write the fraction shown by a pizza cut into $8$ equal slices with $3$ slices eaten.

The whole pizza has $8$ equal parts, so the denominator is $8$. Three parts are eaten, so the numerator is $3$.
$$\text{fraction eaten} = \dfrac{3}{8}$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• The denominator tells you the size of each part; the numerator tells you how many of those parts you have.
• Fractions are exact values, unlike rounded decimals.
• Always read $\dfrac{a}{b}$ as "$a$ out of $b$ equal parts".

✅ Check
In $\dfrac{5}{6}$, the numerator is $5$ and the denominator is $6$; this is a proper fraction because $5 < 6$.

notes.heading: Equivalent Fractions and Simplifying
notes.body:
Equivalent fractions look different but represent exactly the same amount. Simplifying means writing a fraction using the smallest possible whole numbers.

📌 Definition
Equivalent fractions are fractions that have the same value but different numerators and denominators.

$$\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{4}{8} = \dfrac{50}{100}$$

🔑 Key Concept
You can create an equivalent fraction by multiplying or dividing both the numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number.

$$\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{a \times k}{b \times k} = \dfrac{a \div k}{b \div k}$$

Simplifying uses division by the highest common factor (HCF) of the numerator and denominator.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Finding equivalent fractions
Find three fractions equivalent to $\dfrac{2}{3}$.

Multiply numerator and denominator by $2$, $3$, and $5$:
$$\dfrac{2 \times 2}{3 \times 2} = \dfrac{4}{6}, \quad \dfrac{2 \times 3}{3 \times 3} = \dfrac{6}{9}, \quad \dfrac{2 \times 5}{3 \times 5} = \dfrac{10}{15}$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Simplifying a fraction
Simplify $\dfrac{18}{24}$.

Step 1: Find the HCF of $18$ and $24$.
Factors of $18$: $1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18$
Factors of $24$: $1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24$
The HCF is $6$.

Step 2: Divide numerator and denominator by $6$.
$$\dfrac{18 \div 6}{24 \div 6} = \dfrac{3}{4}$$

So $\dfrac{18}{24}$ simplifies to $\dfrac{3}{4}$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Adding or subtracting the same number to the numerator and denominator. This does NOT give an equivalent fraction. Only multiplication or division by the same number works.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• A fraction is in its simplest form when the HCF of the numerator and denominator is $1$.
• Simplifying does not change the value of the fraction.
• You can simplify in stages if you cannot spot the HCF immediately.

✅ Tip
To check whether two fractions are equivalent, cross-multiply: if $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d}$, then $a \times d = b \times c$.

notes.heading: Mixed Numbers and Improper Fractions
notes.body:
Mixed numbers and improper fractions are two ways of writing values larger than one whole. Being able to convert between them is essential for calculations and for comparing quantities.

📌 Definitions
• A mixed number has a whole-number part and a fraction part. Example: $2\dfrac{1}{3}$.
• An improper fraction has a numerator that is greater than or equal to its denominator. Example: $\dfrac{7}{3}$.

🔑 How it works
To convert a mixed number to an improper fraction:
1. Multiply the whole number by the denominator.
2. Add the numerator.
3. Write the result over the original denominator.

$$a\dfrac{b}{c} = \dfrac{a \times c + b}{c}$$

To convert an improper fraction to a mixed number:
1. Divide the numerator by the denominator.
2. The quotient becomes the whole number.
3. The remainder becomes the new numerator.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Mixed to improper
Write $3\dfrac{2}{5}$ as an improper fraction.

$$3\dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{3 \times 5 + 2}{5} = \dfrac{15 + 2}{5} = \dfrac{17}{5}$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Improper to mixed
Write $\dfrac{23}{4}$ as a mixed number.

$23 \div 4 = 5$ remainder $3$, so:
$$\dfrac{23}{4} = 5\dfrac{3}{4}$$

⚠️ Common Misconception
Thinking that $3\dfrac{2}{5}$ means $3 \times \dfrac{2}{5}$. It actually means $3 + \dfrac{2}{5}$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Use mixed numbers for measurements and everyday descriptions.
• Use improper fractions when multiplying or dividing.
• Always check that the fraction part of a mixed number is proper.

✅ Check
$4\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{9}{2}$ and $\dfrac{11}{3} = 3\dfrac{2}{3}$.

notes.heading: Comparing and Ordering Fractions
notes.body:
To compare fractions, you need to express them using the same denominator or convert them to decimals. This skill is useful whenever you need to decide which quantity is larger.

📌 Definition
When two fractions have the same denominator, the one with the larger numerator is the larger fraction.

🔑 Key Concept
To compare fractions with different denominators, find a common denominator — usually the lowest common multiple (LCM) of the denominators. Then rewrite each fraction with that denominator and compare numerators.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Same denominator
Which is larger, $\dfrac{5}{8}$ or $\dfrac{3}{8}$?

Both have denominator $8$, and $5 > 3$, so:
$$\dfrac{5}{8} > \dfrac{3}{8}$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Different denominators
Which is larger, $\dfrac{2}{3}$ or $\dfrac{3}{5}$?

Step 1: Find the LCM of $3$ and $5$, which is $15$.

Step 2: Rewrite each fraction.
$$\dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{2 \times 5}{3 \times 5} = \dfrac{10}{15}$$
$$\dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{3 \times 3}{5 \times 3} = \dfrac{9}{15}$$

Step 3: Compare numerators.
$$\dfrac{10}{15} > \dfrac{9}{15} \quad \text{so} \quad \dfrac{2}{3} > \dfrac{3}{5}$$

💡 Worked Example 3 — Using benchmarks
Is $\dfrac{7}{12}$ greater than $\dfrac{1}{2}$?

$$\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{6}{12}$$
Since $\dfrac{7}{12} > \dfrac{6}{12}$, the fraction is greater than one half.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Comparing only the numerators or only the denominators when the denominators are different. $\dfrac{2}{3}$ is larger than $\dfrac{3}{5}$, even though $5 > 3$.

✅ Tip
When comparing a fraction to $\dfrac{1}{2}$, double the numerator. If the result is greater than the denominator, the fraction is larger than $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

notes.heading: Adding and Subtracting Fractions
notes.body:
Adding and subtracting fractions requires the same denominator, just as you can only add things that are measured in the same unit.

📌 Definition
Fractions can be added or subtracted directly only when they share a common denominator.

🔑 How it works
1. If the denominators are the same, add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator.
2. If the denominators are different, find a common denominator (preferably the LCM).
3. Rewrite each fraction with the common denominator.
4. Add or subtract the numerators.
5. Simplify the answer if possible.

$$\dfrac{a}{c} + \dfrac{b}{c} = \dfrac{a + b}{c}$$

💡 Worked Example 1 — Same denominator
Find $\dfrac{5}{9} + \dfrac{2}{9}$.

$$\dfrac{5}{9} + \dfrac{2}{9} = \dfrac{5 + 2}{9} = \dfrac{7}{9}$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Different denominators
Find $\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{6}$.

Step 1: The LCM of $4$ and $6$ is $12$.

Step 2: Rewrite each fraction.
$$\dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{3}{12}, \quad \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{2}{12}$$

Step 3: Add.
$$\dfrac{3}{12} + \dfrac{2}{12} = \dfrac{5}{12}$$

💡 Worked Example 3 — Subtraction with mixed numbers
Find $2\dfrac{3}{5} - 1\dfrac{4}{5}$.

Step 1: The fraction part $\dfrac{3}{5} - \dfrac{4}{5}$ is not possible, so borrow $1$ whole from the $2$.
$$2\dfrac{3}{5} = 1\dfrac{8}{5}$$

Step 2: Subtract.
$$1\dfrac{8}{5} - 1\dfrac{4}{5} = \dfrac{4}{5}$$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Adding the denominators together. The denominator stays the same once the fractions share a common denominator.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Never add or subtract denominators.
• Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions if it makes the calculation easier.
• Always simplify your final answer.

✅ Check
Estimate: $\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{6}$ is about $0.25 + 0.17 = 0.42$, and $\dfrac{5}{12} \approx 0.42$.

notes.heading: Multiplying and Dividing Fractions
notes.body:
Multiplication and division of fractions are often easier than addition and subtraction because you do not need a common denominator. These operations are used when scaling recipes, finding fractions of amounts, and sharing quantities.

📌 Definition
To multiply two fractions, multiply the numerators together and multiply the denominators together.

$$\dfrac{a}{b} \times \dfrac{c}{d} = \dfrac{a \times c}{b \times d}$$

🔑 How Division Works
Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. The reciprocal of $\dfrac{a}{b}$ is $\dfrac{b}{a}$.

$$\dfrac{a}{b} \div \dfrac{c}{d} = \dfrac{a}{b} \times \dfrac{d}{c}$$

💡 Worked Example 1 — Multiplying fractions
Find $\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{5}{7}$.

$$\dfrac{2 \times 5}{3 \times 7} = \dfrac{10}{21}$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Cancelling before multiplying
Find $\dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{8}{9}$.

Cancel the $3$ with the $9$ and the $4$ with the $8$:
$$\dfrac{^{\,1}\cancel{3}}{_{\,1}\cancel{4}} \times \dfrac{^{\,2}\cancel{8}}{_{\,3}\cancel{9}} = \dfrac{1 \times 2}{1 \times 3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$$

💡 Worked Example 3 — Dividing fractions
Find $\dfrac{5}{6} \div \dfrac{2}{3}$.

Step 1: Multiply by the reciprocal of $\dfrac{2}{3}$, which is $\dfrac{3}{2}$.
$$\dfrac{5}{6} \div \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{5}{6} \times \dfrac{3}{2}$$

Step 2: Multiply and simplify.
$$\dfrac{5 \times 3}{6 \times 2} = \dfrac{15}{12} = \dfrac{5}{4} = 1\dfrac{1}{4}$$

⚠️ Common Mistake
Trying to find a common denominator before multiplying or dividing. That step is only needed for addition and subtraction.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• "Of" usually means multiply: $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of $12$ means $\dfrac{1}{3} \times 12$.
• Cancel common factors before multiplying to keep numbers small.
• A whole number can be written as a fraction with denominator $1$.

✅ Tip
To divide by a whole number, multiply by its reciprocal: $\dfrac{a}{b} \div 5 = \dfrac{a}{b} \times \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{a}{5b}$.

notes.heading: Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
notes.body:
Fractions, decimals, and percentages are three ways of representing the same value. Being able to move between them helps you choose the most convenient form for a calculation. This note focuses on the fraction perspective; for a deeper focus on percentage applications, see the dedicated percentages topic.

📌 Definitions
• A fraction shows parts of a whole: $\dfrac{3}{4}$.
• A decimal uses place value based on tenths, hundredths, and so on: $0.75$.
• A percentage is a fraction out of $100$: $75\%$.

🔑 How it works
Fraction to decimal: divide the numerator by the denominator.
$$\dfrac{3}{4} = 3 \div 4 = 0.75$$

Decimal to fraction: write the decimal over a power of ten and simplify.
$$0.6 = \dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{3}{5}$$

Fraction to percentage: first convert to a decimal, then multiply by $100$.
$$\dfrac{3}{5} = 0.6 = 60\%$$

💡 Worked Example 1 — Fraction to decimal
Write $\dfrac{7}{8}$ as a decimal.

$$7 \div 8 = 0.875$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Repeating decimal
Write $\dfrac{1}{3}$ as a decimal.

$$1 \div 3 = 0.333\ldots = 0.\dot{3}$$

This is a recurring decimal because the digit $3$ repeats forever.

💡 Worked Example 3 — Fraction of an amount
Find $\dfrac{3}{4}$ of £28.

Step 1: Divide by the denominator.
$$28 \div 4 = 7$$

Step 2: Multiply by the numerator.
$$7 \times 3 = 21$$

So $\dfrac{3}{4}$ of £28 is £21.

⚠️ Common Misconception
Thinking that $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of an amount is the same as dividing by $3$ and then multiplying by $1$, which is true, but forgetting that $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of the amount means dividing by $3$ and multiplying by $2$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Learn the common conversions: $\dfrac{1}{2}=0.5=50\%$, $\dfrac{1}{4}=0.25=25\%$, $\dfrac{3}{4}=0.75=75\%$, $\dfrac{1}{5}=0.2=20\%$, $\dfrac{1}{10}=0.1=10\%$.
• A fraction is exact; a decimal may be rounded.
• To find a fraction of an amount, divide by the denominator and multiply by the numerator.

✅ Check
$\dfrac{2}{5} = 0.4 = 40\%$, so 40% of £30 = 0.4 × 30 = £12.

questions.stem: In the fraction $\dfrac{7}{12}$, what is the denominator?
questions.explanation: The denominator is the bottom number of a fraction; it tells you how many equal parts the whole is divided into. Here it is $12$.

questions.stem: Which of these is an improper fraction?
questions.explanation: An improper fraction has a numerator that is greater than or equal to its denominator. Since $7 = 7$, $\dfrac{7}{7}$ is improper.
The HCF of $15$ and $25$ is $5$. Dividing both numerator and denominator by $5$ gives $\dfrac{3}{5}$.

questions.stem: What is $\dfrac{17}{5}$ as a mixed number?

questions.explanation: Multiplying numerator and denominator of $\dfrac{3}{4}$ by $3$ gives $\dfrac{9}{12}$, so the two fractions are equivalent.
Using the common denominator $15$, $\dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{10}{15}$ and $\dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{9}{15}$. Since $\dfrac{10}{15} > \dfrac{9}{15}$, we have $\dfrac{2}{3} > \dfrac{3}{5}$.

When denominators are the same, add the numerators and keep the denominator: $\dfrac{3}{8} + \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{4}{8}$. This can be simplified to $\dfrac{1}{2}$, but $\dfrac{4}{8}$ is the direct result.
The LCM of $6$ and $4$ is $12$. Rewriting gives $\dfrac{10}{12} - \dfrac{3}{12} = \dfrac{7}{12}$.
Multiplying gives $\dfrac{2 \times 3}{5 \times 4} = \dfrac{6}{20}$. Simplifying by dividing numerator and denominator by $2$ gives $\dfrac{3}{10}$.
Dividing by $\dfrac{2}{3}$ is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal $\dfrac{3}{2}$: $\dfrac{4}{9} \times \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{12}{18} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.
Divide $64$ by $8$ to get $8$, then multiply by $3$ to get $24$. So $\dfrac{3}{8}$ of $64 = 24$.
$5 \div 8 = 0.625$. This is an exact decimal because the denominator $8$ is a power of $2$.

questions.stem: A recipe needs $\dfrac{3}{4}$ cup of flour for one batch. How much flour is needed for $2\dfrac{1}{2}$ batches?
A piece of ribbon $2\dfrac{1}{4}$ metres long is cut into pieces that are $\dfrac{3}{4}$ metre each. How many pieces are there?
A water tank is $\dfrac{5}{6}$ full. After $30$ litres are used, it is $\dfrac{2}{3}$ full. What is the total capacity of the tank?
questions.explanation: The fraction used is $\dfrac{5}{6} - \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{5}{6} - \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{1}{6}$. This $\dfrac{1}{6}$ of the tank equals $30$ litres, so the full capacity is $30 \times 6 = 180$ litres.
